changes.before: Change the unit attribute to hours. Does the numeric storage convert?
changes.after: An attribute is extra information attached to an R object. Adding a label does not convert the measurements.

before: attr(x, name) reads a named attribute; assigning through it attaches metadata. Attributes can record names, dimensions, class or a custom unit. This custom unit label does not itself convert numbers or enforce a unit system.

typeof reports the underlying R type. class reports the class used by many higher-level operations; setting a class label does not validate that the object satisfies its intended contract. Special attributes can alter interpretation without replacing the stored numbers.

class takes an object and reports its higher-level class label. For this ordinary double vector the label is numeric, while typeof reports the storage type double.
```r
values <- c(10, 20)
cat(class(values), "\n", sep = "")
cat(typeof(values), "\n", sep = "")
```
It prints:
```text
numeric
double
```

Complete local R example; the app itself does not execute it:
```r
values <- c(10, 20)
attr(values, "unit") <- "minutes"
cat(attr(values, "unit"), "\n")
cat(typeof(values), "\n")
```

Expected output or behavior: minutes
double. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
